column1: # Contextual cases for the class-bigram experiment (spellless/wordclass.lua).
# Not in tests/cases/, and deliberately: those files are the contract, this one
# is a measurement of a feature that is off by default.  bench/context.lua runs
# `behind` is the text in front of the caret, with `_` for a space and `-` for
# nothing at all.  It is fed to preceding.previous_word, so the gating -- one
# space, no punctuation, a dictionary word -- is exercised end to end.
# `kind` is what the row is for:
#   fix    a morphological-sibling failure from tests/cases: the intended word
#          is not first today, and the question is whether context makes it so.
#   keep   an answer that is already first: it must stay first.
#   null   the context must change the candidate list not at all.
# `expected` is the word that must be at rank 1, or `=raw` for the literal
# input, or `=same` meaning the whole 20-candidate list must be identical to
# the one produced with no context at all.
# HOW THE PREVIOUS WORDS WERE CHOSEN, which is the only thing that makes this
# The `fix` rows are every one of the 40 cases in tests/cases/*.tsv where the
# intended word is not first AND the word that beat it shares a four-character
# prefix with it -- the morphological-sibling class of docs/ALGORITHM.md §6.
# The inputs and the intended words are therefore not chosen at all: they are
# whatever the existing case files already assert.  Only the previous word is
# mine, and the rule I followed was "what would a person actually have typed
# immediately before this word", written down for all forty before the ranking
# Several of them are honestly bad for the feature and were left that way:
# "the regulatory" and "the regulator" are both perfectly good English, so a
# determiner cannot separate them and the row is expected to stay broken; the
# are words the hand-written table has no opinion about at all.  Choosing more
# convenient contexts for those would have measured nothing.
# Answers that are first today, in contexts a person would really have typed.
# The previous word is a classified one wherever English allows it, because a
# previous word the table has no opinion about tests nothing.
# The literal has to stay reachable and leading whatever is behind it.
# Contexts that are wrong for the word on purpose: a contraction after a
# determiner is not English, and must still not be demoted.
# Every gate, and the two previous words that are supposed to say nothing.
